subject: Biology
questionText: State any three universal rules followed while writing biological names.
questionLatex: \text{State any three universal rules followed while writing biological names.}

answer.value: The universal rules of nomenclature are: (i) Biological names are generally in Latin and written in italics. (ii) The first word represents the genus while the second component denotes the specific epithet. (iii) Both the words in a biological name, when handwritten, are separately underlined, or printed in italics to indicate their Latin origin. (iv) The first word denoting the genus starts with a capital letter while the specific epithet starts with a small letter.

subject: Biology

questionLatex: \text{Define classification in biology.}

subject: Biology
questionText: What is a taxonomic category?
questionLatex: $$\text{What is a taxonomic category?}$$

subject: Biology
questionText: Define species according to taxonomic studies.
questionLatex: $$\text{Define species according to taxonomic studies.}$$

subject: Biology
questionText: The lowest taxonomic category in the classification hierarchy is:
questionLatex: $$\text{The lowest taxonomic category in the classification hierarchy is:}$$
